Subject: Helm values & CI sanity for private deploy (review requested)

Hi all —

Quick request: I'm consolidating the Helm values and CI expectations for the upcoming private deployment (VPC/on-prem bundle) that Acme will run in their air-gapped cluster. During the last dry run we saw three classes of breakage:

- mismatched value names across module charts (service.port vs svc.port) causing templating failures
- secrets/credential paths in values that assume cloud KMS paths rather than customer KMS mapping
- CI jobs that pull from public registries (fails in air-gapped environments) and missing helm test hooks

What I'm asking for: please review the attached artifacts and call out any blockers by EOD Monday (2026-08-17). Focus areas:

1) Helm values contract (schema + required vs optional keys) — should be a simple JSON schema we can validate in CI
2) Secrets handling and KMS path abstraction (avoid hardcoded cloud paths)
3) CI gating: dry-run/helm template, helm test, image/promote flow for registry mirroring, and preflight ansible idempotency checks for on-prem nodes
4) Version pinning/compat matrix for chart dependencies and CRDs

Attachments: helm-values-diff.csv (extracted diffs between current charts), ci-pipeline-snippets.yml (recommended pipeline stage snippets).
Link: https://drive.redwood/company/privdeploy/helm-values-contract.docx
JIRA: JIRA-INFRA-4123 (tracking fixes)

Proposed short timeline: get owners & comments today, push small fixes Tuesday, run a focused preflight Wednesday with Acme.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Manager, Deployment Safety
Redwood Inference

---
Note: I referenced the on-prem ansible playbook that Marcus maintains — Marcus, flag anything you think will require a separate preflight playbook change.

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: bethany.cole@acme.com, ops@acme.com
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 11:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Helm values & CI sanity for private deploy (review requested)

Thanks Soojin — quick pass below. I've attached a suggested-values.patch with small name normalizations and a proposed minimal schema. High level:

- Values schema: create a top-level schema file (helm-values-schema.json) and add a CI validation step that runs `helm template --validate` plus `ajv` schema check for required keys. This catches the service.port vs svc.port problem early.
- Secrets: introduce `secrets.kms_path` as the single canonical mapping for secret fetches. For customers using their own KMS, CI should accept a mapping file (kms-mapping.yaml) that converts `redwood/kms/path` -> `acme/kms/path`.
- Node selectors / tolerations: remove any hardcoded selectors in upstream charts; push them into a deployment overlay values file that the ansible playbook injects during on-prem pushes.
- Registry handling for airgap: add a pipeline step to mirror images and charts into the customer's internal registry. In CI, fail fast if registry mirror step is not present for air-gapped accounts.
- Helm tests: add `helm test` to the post-deploy stage for canary namespaces and set timeout to 5m.
- Ansible: ensure all playbooks are idempotent and add a `--check` dry-run stage in the playbook CI job. Avoid any `--force`/destructive steps without explicit approval.

Minor: pin mux-chart v1.3.2 to avoid transient CRD changes until we test. Also propose a small Makefile target `make helm-validate` that runs the schema + template checks locally.

Attached: suggested-values.patch

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Appreciate this level of detail — a couple notes from Acme side:

- We are fully air-gapped. Any CI stage that pulls directly from public helm repos or public container registries will fail in our environment. We do have an internal registry and an internal chart museum that your pipeline will need to mirror into.
- KMS: our key rotation window occurs every 30 days; we need an automated stub in the ansible playbook to handle key refresh mapping during deployment windows.
- Our security team requires a sign-off checklist that includes: schema validation pass, secrets mapping documented, canary tests green for 3 consecutive runs, and a rollback playbook verified.

Can you produce a short checklist we can use for sign-off? Also confirm whether the `make helm-validate` target will run locally for our engineers before they push changes to mirror registries.

Thanks — Bethany
Bethany Cole
Platform Engineering Manager
Acme Payments
